33914-myology-and-serology-of-the-avian-:
William B. Stallcup published this 1954 study of finches in the University of Kansas Museum of Natural History series. It joins two kinds of evidence: the muscles of the leg and pelvic region, and blood tests that compare related birds. Specimens were preserved, dissected under a low-power microscope, and tested with antigens and antisera.

Stallcup reviews earlier work by Hudson, Fisher, and Berger, then sets out his own findings on muscle form and blood kinship. Tables and figures support the text, and a summary closes the study. The paper serves bird students who want a careful, technical look at how finch groups relate.
doe-osti-3015581-radioactivity-in-materi:
A University of Kentucky final report under award DE-SC0024666 sums up screening detector materials for stray radioactivity. It covers August 2024 to August 2025. Ryan MacLellan leads the materials screening work for nEXO. That is a proposed ton-scale experiment hunting neutrinoless double-beta decay in xenon-136. A single radioactive contaminant can fake the signal there.

Kentucky runs an ultra-low-background gamma-ray spectrometer. It also manages low-background counting project-wide. A catalog of almost 300 radioassay measurements is in final collaboration review. Some are among the most sensitive ever made for the parts tested. The catalog goes next to Physical Review C. The report also notes the only polonium-210 measurement the group has made with a germanium detector. Two doctoral students defended in 2025 under the award.
podcast-joerogan-gzAQ7SklDxo:
Brian Muraresku and Graham Hancock join the Joe Rogan Experience together for episode 1543. Muraresku wrote The Immortality Key, arguing that ancient religions used psychedelic sacraments. Hancock, the lost-civilization author, sees a kindred case in his own field. Rogan pairs two rebels in one room.

They lay out the claim that the roots of Western religion run through drug-laced rites, from Eleusis in Greece to the early church. Rogan asks what proof survives and where the case is thinnest. The episode is a rich, strange talk at the crossroads of archaeology and the sacred, with two authors feeding each other's fire.
podcast-joerogan-w8Q6CWv7IXo:
Philosopher Sam Harris has his first long talk with Joe Rogan in episode 543 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Harris, author of The End of Faith and Waking Up, is known for sharp arguments against religion and for his work on meditation. This early marathon started a long Rogan saga.

The two debate free will, the self, and whether science can ground moral values. Harris presents his view that the feeling of free choice is an illusion. Rogan plays the curious layman, testing each claim with everyday cases. Thinkers who enjoy calm, clear argument will find the pair well matched here.
